subject.title: [Feature]: Skill author-defined setup hook (run skill-supplied script on install/update)

question: Should OpenClaw add a core install/update lifecycle hook for skill-authored `setup.script`, or keep setup execution outside core through the published ClawHub/admin-RPC plugin path until SDK and security contracts mature?
rationale: The implementation choice decides whether downloaded skill metadata can cause host script execution during install/update and what env, consent, logging, timeout, and ClawHub trust contracts become public.

options.title: Stabilize plugin path first
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers harden the ClawHub/admin-RPC plugin route and land the installed-skill SDK helpers needed to avoid copied security logic.

options.title: Sponsor opt-in core hook
options.body: Approve a default-off core lifecycle hook with explicit install/update opt-in, shared host-exec env policy, path containment, timeout policy, docs, and live install/update proof.

options.title: Decline automatic execution
options.body: Close the core lifecycle request as not planned and document that skill setup scripts must be run only through explicit admin/plugin workflows.

recommendation.title: Stabilize plugin path first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers harden the ClawHub/admin-RPC plugin route and land the installed-skill SDK helpers needed to avoid copied security logic.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved decision is primarily an install-time host execution and env/security boundary, and this person is tied to the current operator install policy path.
